outcome: The general conjecture (arbitrary non-hyperelliptic curves) remains open; work since 26 January 2024 only re-proves or extends the already-settled generic case, so no change to the stated bullet was found.
summary: Green's conjecture as Wikipedia states it (26 Jan 2024 revision) is about an arbitrary non-hyperelliptic curve: its Clifford index equals the extent to which its canonical embedding has linear syzygies. This is a much stronger, and still-open, statement than the 'generic curve' case, which Voisin resolved in the early 2000s (a fact predating the window). I searched for any work since 26 January 2024 bearing on the general statement, the generic case, or related variants. Two relevant post-snapshot preprints turned up: (1) Michael Kemeny, 'A proof of generic Green's conjecture in odd genus' (arXiv:2502.09735, submitted 13 Feb 2025, v4 10 Dec 2025), which gives a new, computation-avoiding proof of Voisin's existing odd-genus generic-curve theorem — it re-proves a known result rather than extending it to new curves, so it is not a change to the general conjecture nor even new territory in the generic case. (2) Yi Wei, 'Generic Green's Conjecture and Generic Geometric Syzygy Conjecture in Positive Characteristic' (arXiv:2109.12187, originally 2021, latest v4 13 May 2025), which proves the generic conjecture in positive characteristic p ≥ (g+4)/2 and a case of the related Geometric Syzygy Conjecture for even genus — this is a different setting (positive characteristic) than the classical statement (implicitly characteristic 0) and, per §3.1, changing the ground field/characteristic makes this a related-problem variant rather than a restriction (case) of the stated bullet, since the bullet does not specify or vary over characteristic and the classical open problem is understood over the complex numbers / characteristic 0. Neither paper touches the arbitrary (non-generic) curve case, which the Wikipedia article and this search confirm is still explicitly open ('The conjecture for arbitrary curves remains open'). I found no counterexample, no resolution, and no AI involvement anywhere in this area: neither paper mentions AI, ML, or automated theorem-proving tools, and a targeted search for AI-related work touching Green's conjecture returned nothing relevant (only unrelated hits about 'Green's functions' in PDE/ML contexts, and a blog post about AI counterexamples to unrelated conjectures — Erdős unit distance, a Grothendieck group-schemes question, and the Jacobian conjecture — which does not mention Green's conjecture at all). Given the clear, explicit statement on Wikipedia's own article that the general conjecture is open, and the absence of any preprint, announcement, or database entry claiming otherwise, I am confident nothing has happened to the general conjecture within the window, and certainly no AI involvement.
competing_reading: One could argue the positive-characteristic result (arXiv:2109.12187) is a genuine partial advance if one reads 'non-hyperelliptic curve' in the bullet as agnostic to the base field, in which case settling the generic case in positive characteristic could count as `partial` progress on a (field-restricted) case of the general conjecture. I judge this unlikely to be the intended reading: the conjecture as classically posed and as linked from Wikipedia is about complex projective curves, and the positive-characteristic problem is treated in the literature as its own conjecture (with separate statements and its own history of partial results long before 2024), i.e. a related problem sharing the name rather than a sub-case of the stated one. Also, even under the generous reading, this would only be a case of the *generic*-curve sub-problem, not of the arbitrary-curve statement actually in the bullet, so it would still not touch what the bullet asks.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement proving (or disproving) the Clifford-index/syzygy equivalence for a genuinely non-generic, non-hyperelliptic curve (or a stated counterexample among such curves) would settle whether real progress occurred; absent that, the status stands as open with no change.
